author: Vitor
notes: Introduced bug when checking for a sum value of 0 before adding combinations.
aiExplanation: This solution solves **"paths with max score"** on a grid using **dynamic programming**, walking backwards from the bottom-right cell to the top-left and, for each cell, storing a pair `[maxScore, pathCount]` built from the best of its three neighbors (down, right, diagonal); however, it has a bug where `combs` is forced to `0` whenever the neighbors' `max` score happens to be `0`, which incorrectly discards valid zero-score paths and causes the solution to fail.

author: Vitor
notes: First accepted solution, disorganized code. Following submissions attempt to improve on performance.
aiExplanation: This is the same **bottom-right-to-top-left dynamic programming** approach as before, building a `[maxScore, pathCount]` pair for each cell from its down, right, and diagonal neighbors, but it fixes the earlier bug by always summing the `pathCount` of whichever neighbors match the `max` score, instead of incorrectly zeroing out `combs` when `max` is `0`.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This solution keeps the same **dynamic programming** logic for finding the max-score path count on the grid, but tidies up the code by computing the last row and last column with concise ternary expressions and by destructuring each neighbor's `[score, count]` pair into named variables (`bs`/`bc`, `rs`/`rc`, `ds`/`dc`) before comparing them to find the `max` and summing matching `combs`.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This is a minor variant of the previous **dynamic programming** solution that keeps each neighbor's `[score, count]` pair as a whole array (`b`, `r`, `d`) instead of destructuring it into separate variables, accessing `b[0]`/`b[1]` and so on directly when computing the `max` score and the matching `combs` count for each cell.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This solution again implements the same **dynamic programming** approach over the grid, computing each cell's `[maxScore, pathCount]` from its down, right, and diagonal neighbors, but restructures the innermost logic to use an `if`/`else` block instead of an early `continue` when a cell contains an obstacle (`'X'`).

author: Vitor
notes: Amplified space to n + 1 to remove preparation for first row/column, making the code much cleaner. Problem does not have enough tests to accurately measure performance.
aiExplanation: This is a more streamlined version of the same **dynamic programming** algorithm: instead of special-casing the last row and column, it pads the `dp` table with one extra row and column of zeros (acting as a natural boundary) and marks the bottom-right cell of the board as `'0'` so a single unified loop can compute the `[maxScore, pathCount]` for every cell, including the start, by comparing its down, right, and diagonal neighbors.
